title: Transportable Framework Authority
purpose: Defines durable repository-local Git-object evidence that allows an initialized repository to prove initializer-managed framework material against exact accepted repo-spec revisions after transport away from the originating framework checkout.

normative_requirements.text: For each accepted framework reconciliation lineage revision governed by this contract, the initialized repository shall maintain a deterministic repository-local framework-authority bundle at `repo/initializer/framework-authority/<framework-sha1>/`, where `<framework-sha1>` is the exact lowercase SHA-1 object ID of that accepted framework commit.

A framework-authority bundle shall retain the exact Git commit object identified by the corresponding accepted lineage revision and the minimal tree/blob object closure necessary to resolve the authoritative initialization inventory endpoints and framework source objects required to prove initializer-managed `repo/` material for that revision.

Every retained Git object shall be locally verifiable by recomputing its canonical Git object identity from object type, byte length, and uncompressed content; the bundle shall fail validation when any retained object's computed identity differs from its stored object ID.

Framework-authority verification shall begin from the exact accepted lineage commit object ID and traverse only cryptographically linked Git tree/blob identities to resolve required inventory and source content; a repository-local index, manifest, path list, digest list, or other sidecar metadata shall be subordinate evidence and shall not independently authorize managed content.

The retained object closure shall be sufficient to determine the initializer-managed `repo/` destination authority relevant to the accepted state, including authoritative inventory identity, stable managed-material correspondence, exact source blob bytes, executable/non-executable mode where governed, and historical managed paths needed to distinguish authorized transition from unrelated committed repository drift.

The bundle representation and any subordinate index shall be deterministically serialized/stored so equivalent accepted framework identity and authoritative inventory/source content produce equivalent repository-local authority content.

Routine validation of a promoted initialized repository shall be able to verify framework-managed repository integrity using only the promoted repository's committed lineage and framework-authority bundles; it shall not require the originating local repo-spec checkout and shall not retrieve framework authority from a network or remote repository.

Missing, malformed, incomplete, internally inconsistent, unanchored, or tampered framework-authority evidence required for the accepted lineage state shall fail closed; coordinated modification of managed content and subordinate local metadata shall not be sufficient to produce a valid authority proof.

When an initialized repository has accepted lineage entries that predate this framework-authority representation, a later governed upgrade may materialize the missing historical bundles only from the exact locally resolvable framework repository/revision identities already recorded by accepted lineage or valid legacy provenance; unresolved history shall not be guessed and remote retrieval is not authorized.

A prospective reconciliation-target framework-authority bundle, together with any required exact historical backfill, shall be present in the staged candidate before complete staged validation; non-promoted attempts shall not advance accepted lineage or accepted framework-authority state.

conformance.rationale: Current accepted repo-spec authority declares no governed generic product implementation-test obligation for this requirement at product/scripts/test-product; source-development tests and validation self-tests are separate surfaces. Future activation requires a governed correspondence update.
